title: Abdullah ibn Umar
hook: followed the Prophet's footsteps so closely he prayed where he had prayed

segments.voice: Yesterday: Anas ibn Malik, ten years in the Prophet's house and never scolded, not even an uff. Your line was ten years, no scolding.

On the long road between Medina and Mecca there are spots with nothing special about them. A bend. A tree. A patch of ground by a valley. Travelers pass them without a glance. One traveler kept stopping. Nafi', who learned from him, tells it in Sahih al-Bukhari: Abdullah ibn Umar would halt at certain places and pray there, because he had seen the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, pray in those very places. Today: the son of Umar, walking in someone else's footprints.
screen: `A BEND, A TREE, A VALLEY.` → `HE STOPPED AND PRAYED.` → `BECAUSE THE PROPHET HAD.`

segments.voice: Abdullah was the son of Umar ibn al-Khattab. What his students passed on was how closely he watched, and how closely he copied. Bukhari gives a whole run of reports from Nafi' naming the places on the pilgrimage road where Ibn Umar prayed, each one a spot where the Prophet had prayed before him. Another scene in Bukhari shows what kind of follower he was. As a young man, Abdullah slept in the mosque. He dreamed that two angels took him to the Fire, and he was afraid. He told his sister Hafsah, and she told the Prophet, who said: what an excellent man Abdullah is, if only he would pray at night. His son Salim adds one line: after that, Abdullah slept only a little of the night. One sentence of praise, one gentle if only, and the shape of his nights changed. Later scholars asked what kind of following this was. Some distinguish between what the Prophet did as worship and teaching, and what he did simply as a traveler, such as where he happened to stop. Some readers see Ibn Umar following both kinds, out of love. Either way, the picture stays: a man who wanted his feet to land where the footsteps were.
screen: `THE SON OF UMAR.` · `PLACES ON THE PILGRIM ROAD.` · `IF ONLY HE PRAYED AT NIGHT.` · `WORSHIP, OR JUST WHERE HE STOPPED?` · then, large: `IN HIS FOOTSTEPS.`

segments.voice: Choose one small sunnah, a habit the Prophet is reported to have kept, that you'll actually do: some Muslims begin with smiling at people they meet, entering the mosque right foot first, as Ibn Umar himself is reported to have done, saying bismillah before they eat, or giving with the right hand. Picture the moment it will happen, and see yourself doing it. If you pray, you can ask to follow well.
Ibn Umar, son of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who prayed where the Prophet had prayed and, after one if only, rose to pray at night. Today's word.
Your line: in his footsteps. Small steps, copied out of love. That's day eight hundred thirty-nine.

howItsDone: Muslims follow the sunnah, the Prophet's example, in worship and in small daily habits; scholars distinguish acts done as worship from those done by custom, and people differ on how far to follow the second kind.

chat.says: Why did Ibn Umar stop to pray at ordinary spots on the road to Mecca?
options: He had seen the Prophet pray in those places, and wanted to follow closely.
Those spots were official stops every pilgrim was required to make.
He believed prayers there counted double, so he never skipped them.
chat.meaning: Nafi' reports in Bukhari that Ibn Umar prayed where he had seen the Prophet pray: a man following in the footsteps.

Nafi'.meaning: a student of Ibn Umar who passed on his reports

Umar ibn al-Khattab.meaning: a leading companion, later caliph; Ibn Umar's father

Hafsah.meaning: Ibn Umar's sister, a wife of the Prophet

sunnah.meaning: the Prophet's example, in worship and daily habits

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 483–492 (Nafi': places on the road where Ibn Umar prayed because the Prophet had)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1121–1122 (the dream; 'what an excellent man Abdullah is, if only he prayed at night'; Salim: he slept little after)
